overpressure.planning.title: Pneumatic Tube Planning
overpressure.planning.1: Tubes build in one go between two endpoints.
overpressure.planning.2: Corner tubes connect at an angle into one smooth tube.
overpressure.planning.3: Place a Pneumatic Connector and rotate it: arrow from
overpressure.planning.4: a chest extracts, arrow into a chest inserts.
overpressure.planning.5: Add an Item Pump to speed up item transport.
overpressure.ponder.curvature_tube.text_: Curved pneumatic tubes are purely visual and may have no collision in some places.
The real tube blocks are invisible and arranged at an angle.
The curved section is treated as one continuous tube path.
overpressure.ponder.pneumatic_connection: Pneumatic connectors decide whether items leave or enter a container.
Extractor mode pulls from the container into the tube line.
Insert mode sends items from the tube line into the container.
Rotate the connector with a wrench to change the side and direction.
Place a filter into an extractor to choose which items it may pull from the container.
A redstone signal disables the extractor. A lit outline means the extractor is blocked.
Items that have already started moving will continue to their destination.
overpressure.ponder.item_pump.text_1: A regular pneumatic line may seem too slow.
overpressure.ponder.item_pump.text_2: Replace the central tube with an Item Pump to accelerate item movement.
overpressure.ponder.item_pump.text_3: The pump does not work by itself.
overpressure.ponder.item_pump.text_4: The pump needs rotation from a cogwheel to start working.
overpressure.ponder.item_pump.text_5: Slow rotation gives the pump a modest transfer speed.
overpressure.ponder.item_pump.text_6: The faster the cogwheel turns, the faster items move through the line.
